articles.title: Mark Winstanley returns to stage after MS diagnosis for Rochdale comedy show
articles.excerpt: Actor Mark Winstanley will perform in 'Cabaret Schmabaret' at the Ukrainian Centre on 19 November, marking his return to the stage after a five-year hiatus due to multiple sclerosis.
articles.content_html:
Actor Mark Winstanley is set to return to the stage after a five-year break following his diagnosis with multiple sclerosis. He will perform in 'Cabaret Schmabaret' at the Ukrainian Centre in Rochdale on 19 November, bringing his comedic talents back to the local audience.

Winstanley, who co-runs the Manchester-based theatre company The Performers’ Playground with Alice Robinson, has a rich history in theatre, having performed nationally and internationally with various touring companies.

His return is particularly significant as it showcases his resilience and commitment to the arts despite his health challenges.

In addition to 'Cabaret Schmabaret', The Performers’ Playground is also fundraising for a separate production of 'Ubu Royale', which is currently in research and development. This production is designed to accommodate Winstanley's mobility and fatigue issues, with plans for a national tour in 2027.

Winstanley's comeback not only highlights his personal journey but also serves as an inspiration for others facing similar challenges. Local audiences can look forward to enjoying a unique comedic experience while supporting a talented artist's return to the stage.
articles.social_headline: Mark Winstanley returns to the stage in Rochdale after battling MS

evidence_sources.captured_text: Actor returns to stage after MS diagnosis for Rochdale comedy show | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch Actor returns to stage after MS diagnosis for Rochdale comedy show David Murphy News Editor November 1, 2026 | just now Print Actor Mark Winstanley is returning to the stage after a five-year gap following his multiple sclerosis diagnosis, with a performance of Cabaret Schmabaret in Rochdale. The Performers’ Playground will bring the comedy show to the Ukrainian Centre on 19 November. The Manchester-based theatre training and performance company is run by Mark and Alice Robinson and specialises in comic live theatre. Before his diagnosis, Mark performed nationally and internationally with touring companies including A Ship of Fools Theatre Company, Vamos Theatre and A Plague of Idiots. The company is also fundraising for a separate production of Ubu Royale , with rehearsals and performances designed around Mark’s impaired mobility and fatigue. The project is in research and development, with plans to share the work this year before a proposed national tour in 2027. Ubu Royale is Neil Bartlett’s translation of Alfred Jarry’s Ubu Roi . It follows Pa Ubu and Ma Ubu, two would-be monarchs whose pursuit of power leads to chaos. The production will feature three performers playing more than 20 characters, using puppetry and a set built from discarded materials and repurposed mobility aids. The company describes it as its most ambitious project to date, combining satire and physical comedy with frequent strong language and bodily humour. Alongside Mark, the cast and creative team includes Susanna Amato, David Nixon, Alice Robinson, Thomas Toppler and Sophie Tyrrell. Mark, Alice, Susanna and David also work as practitioners and teachers. Their collective experience includes work across RADA, Performers College, Ecole Philippe Gaulier, Contact, Cheshire Dance, Uncurbed Collective, Handmade Parade and Driftwood Studio. The team hopes to develop skills in performance, movement, theatre-making, puppetry, mobility and access that they can share with students and other artists. “We want accessibility to be part of the creative process from the very beginning, not something added afterwards. By exploring how ambitious theatre can be made around Mark's access needs, we hope to develop approaches that can benefit not only this production, but the performers and theatre-makers who come after it.” Donations will help fund the production, support its artists and provide the access arrangements needed to make the work possible. articles.title: Rochdale Sixth Form College to host Open Evening on 19 November
articles.excerpt: Prospective students and families are invited to explore courses and meet staff at Rochdale Sixth Form College's Open Evening.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Sixth Form College will host an Open Evening on Thursday, 19 November, from 4pm to 7pm. This event is aimed at prospective students and their families, providing an opportunity to explore the college's offerings and learn more about its academic environment.

Visitors can meet experienced tutors, speak with current Student Ambassadors, and discover the wide range of A level and vocational courses available.

The college is recognised as one of the leading sixth form providers in the UK, particularly noted for its value-added performance, which reflects the progress students make during their studies.

The Principal’s Talk will take place at multiple times throughout the evening, specifically at 4:30pm, 5:15pm, and 6pm. Attendees are encouraged to arrive at the Theatre on the first floor about ten minutes before their chosen session.

There is no need to book a separate place for the talk, allowing flexibility for visitors to attend whichever session suits them best.

To attend the Open Evening, places must be booked in advance. Interested parties can register and find more information by visiting the college's official website.

Please note that there is no on-site parking available, so visitors are advised to check nearby parking options before arriving.

articles.title: Rochdale and Bury see significant increases in driving test pass rates
articles.excerpt: Driving test pass rates in Rochdale and Bury have seen notable increases, with Bury recording a six percentage point rise.
articles.content_html:
Driving test pass rates in Rochdale and Bury have experienced significant increases, according to recent data. Bury recorded a six percentage point rise, bringing its pass rate to 56 percent, the highest in Greater Manchester.

Rochdale also saw improvements, contributing to the overall positive trend in the region.

The increases in pass rates are part of a broader trend across Greater Manchester, where driving test success rates have been on the rise.

This development is particularly beneficial for local residents seeking to obtain their driving licenses, as it may indicate improved driving instruction and testing conditions.

The data highlights the efforts of local driving instructors and testing centres in both Rochdale and Bury, who have been working to enhance the quality of driving education. This could lead to safer roads and more confident drivers in the area.

As the trend continues, it remains to be seen how these improvements will affect the demand for driving lessons and the overall driving culture in the region. Local residents are encouraged to take advantage of the increased pass rates as they pursue their driving qualifications.
articles.social_headline: Driving test pass rates rise in Rochdale and Bury, benefiting local learners.

articles.title: Rochdale remembers as community gathers for Remembrance Day services
articles.excerpt: Members of the public are invited to attend the Remembrance Day services on 8 November 2026, supported by the council.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will hold Remembrance Day services on 8 November 2026, inviting members of the public to join in honouring those who served in the armed forces. The services will take place across various locations in the borough, providing an opportunity for reflection and remembrance.

The council is actively supporting all members of the armed forces community, ensuring that the sacrifices made by service personnel are recognised and commemorated. This initiative aims to foster a sense of unity and respect within the community.

The phrase 'Lest we forget' will resonate throughout the events, reminding attendees of the importance of remembering those who have fought for their country. The council encourages participation from residents to pay tribute to the fallen and show support for veterans.

As the date approaches, further details about specific locations and times for the services will be made available. Residents are encouraged to mark their calendars and participate in this significant occasion.
articles.social_headline: Rochdale invites the community to join Remembrance Day services on 8 November 2026.

articles.excerpt: Temporary road closures will affect Smithy Bridge Road and surrounding areas during early hours on 15 November 2026.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that Smithy Bridge Road in Littleborough will undergo roadworks on Sunday, 15 November 2026.

The work will involve temporary closures of the road either side of the railway level crossing, starting 15 metres northwest of the crossing and extending 40 metres southeast.

The closures will take place from 12:10 am to 5:30 am, impacting traffic flow on Smithy Bridge Road, Milnrow Road, Wildhouse Lane, Kiln Lane, Bridge Street, and Halifax Road (A58).

Local residents and commuters should plan for potential delays and consider alternative routes during these hours. The council advises checking their website for updates and further details on the roadworks.

These roadworks are part of ongoing maintenance efforts to ensure the safety and reliability of local transport infrastructure. Residents are encouraged to stay updated on the developments and any changes to traffic conditions.

articles.title: Rochdale residents return home after gas leak caused by car crash
articles.excerpt: Residents evacuated from Halifax Road in Rochdale can now return home after emergency services contained a gas leak following a car crash.
articles.content_html:
Residents of Halifax Road in Rochdale have been allowed to return to their homes after a car crashed into a house early on Saturday morning, October 31, 2026, causing a gas leak. The incident occurred shortly before 3am, prompting a swift response from emergency services.

Greater Manchester Police reported that they received calls about the collision at around 2:55am. The crash resulted in a confirmed gas leak, leading to the evacuation of approximately 55 residents from nearby properties.

A 50-metre cordon was established while investigations were conducted and safety measures were put in place.

Three fire engines from Rochdale and Littleborough fire stations attended the scene, where firefighters worked to secure the area and assist with evacuations. Two individuals were taken to hospital by the North West Ambulance Service, although their conditions have not been disclosed.

Emergency services remained on-site for about four-and-a-half hours to manage the situation.

Following the containment of the gas leak, Halifax Road has since reopened, allowing residents to return home. This incident underscores the critical role of emergency services in ensuring public safety during unexpected events.

articles.title: Middleton schools face financial challenges due to declining pupil numbers
articles.excerpt: Middleton schools are grappling with financial pressures as a significant drop in birth rates is expected to impact primary school enrolments in 2027.
articles.content_html:
Middleton schools are facing financial challenges as a report reveals a significant decline in birth rates, which is expected to affect primary school enrolments in 2027.

The report, presented to township committees, highlights that the borough is experiencing the lowest birth rate for 23 years, leading to concerns about the long-term financial sustainability of some primary schools.

In September 2026, there was a peak in Reception year pupils, but the projected intake for 2027 is only 2,647, the lowest since 2003.

This decline is anticipated to create additional financial pressures for schools that have already seen a reduction in student numbers and an increase in empty seats over recent years.

The report indicates that while there has been an average of 113 children needing places after moving into the borough each year, this figure has dropped to just 20 over the past two years.

An average of 30 pupils per year have not taken up secondary school places within the borough, exacerbating the situation.

As a response to the declining numbers, Rochdale Council has already removed 90 surplus Reception places for September 2024 and an additional 35 for September 2025.

Further reductions are expected in areas where there are too many empty places, highlighting the need for strategic planning to address these challenges.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Schools face financial challenges over pupil places - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Schools face financial challenges over pupil places The financial and practical challenges surrounding the borough’s school places will be highlighted in each town next week. Rochdale Council’s township committees will hear that the lowest birth rate for 23 years is expected to present a “significant challenge” for the long-term financial sustainability of some primary schools within the borough — while 2027 is expected to see the highest number of students apply for the area’s secondary schools. A report to be presented to Heywood, Pennines, Middleton, Rochdale North and Rochdale South township committees reveals that the borough’s birth rate has seen a peak in Reception year pupils arriving in school in September, 2026, but, the birth rate for the intake in 2027 is 2,647 — the lowest since 2003. The report said: “A small number of schools have seen too many empty seats over the last few years as intake numbers reduced and a low intake in 2027 is going to see additional financial pressures on those schools. “Current birth rates indicate a steady but slow rise in the years to 2030. The current projected intake for 2030 is approximately 2,900 and includes children from new housing developments across the borough.” In September, 2024, 90 surplus Reception places were removed, followed by an additional 35 for September, 2025. The report warns that further reductions are needed in some areas of the borough where there are too many empty places. While recent years have seen an average of 113 children needing places after moving into the borough each year, this figure has fallen to 20 over the past two years. As well as fewer children entering primary schools, there has been an average of 30 pupils per year not taking up secondary school places within the borough. READ MORE: Rugby club unveils new gym as shirt sponsor The report said: “Cumulatively, the net outflow of pupils leaving the borough’s schools has a significant impact on the projection of secondary school numbers. “The current landscape, marked by declining birth rates and a net outflow of pupils, presents a significant challenge for the long-term financial sustainability of some schools within the borough.” In the 2026 secondary school application round, there were 3,113 children in Year 6 applying for transition to secondary school. On offer day, 2,860 pupils were offered places in Rochdale’s secondary schools. Of those offers, 2,485 were offered their first-choice school, 290 were offered a school that they had named as a preference, and 85 were offered a school that was not a preference. A total of 322 children also put as their first preference one of the ten most popular out-of-borough schools. The net number of pupils moving to out of borough this year at transition was 304. This is similar to last year when 310 left for out-of-borough schools. Boroughwide secondary intakes were unexpectedly lower this year. The forecast is for 2027 to be the largest secondary intake year with 3,015 pupils expected to apply to secondary schools within the borough offering 3,060 places. The issues will be highlighted at Heywood Township Committee on Monday, Pennines Township Committee on Tuesday, Rochdale North Township Committee on Wednesday and Middleton Township Committee on Thursday. Rochdale South Township Committee will receive the report the following week on Wednesday, November 11. SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? We’d love to hear it!
